# function: override

Returns a new scheme with the given static values replaced. Every key must already be a static value of the scheme; use `with` to add new ones. The new values are checked against the scheme's component constraints. Replacing a value is explicit on purpose, so a typo or a stale value cannot silently win.

## Example Usage

```terraform
locals {
  dev = provider::naming::scheme(
    "{type}-{system}-{name}-{env}-{region}",
    {
      system = "wha"
      env    = "dev"
      region = "weu"
    },
    {
      env = { allowed = ["dev", "test", "prod"] }
    },
  )

  # `override` replaces a value that is already static. Use `with` to add a new one.
  prod = provider::naming::override(local.dev, { env = "prod" })
}

# rg-wha-net-prod-weu
output "prod_resource_group" {
  value = provider::naming::format(local.prod, { type = "rg", name = "net" })
}
```

## Signature

<!-- signature generated by tfplugindocs -->
```text
override(scheme object, values map of string) object
```

## Arguments

<!-- arguments generated by tfplugindocs -->
1. `scheme` (Object) A scheme, as returned by `scheme`.
1. `values` (Map of String) New values for existing static keys.
